findings.text: Upheld (Q2, logic duplicated). `spokenContract` (binding.ts:207-208) works out the contract to speak after `/v1/me` with the same rule as `refreshContracts` (src/sync/run.ts:102-106): `me.ok ? Math.min(CONTRACT, me.body.contract)`, otherwise `acceptableContract(me.accepted, …)` on a contract refusal. Each file also has its own 5 s deadline constant. I checked this against the code. It is a rule written in two places, not boilerplate. One helper in servers.ts beside `acceptableContract` would hold it.
Advisory (Q1/Q2). The Nothing branch deletes the `names.<state>` flags with its own loop. That repeats `clearName` in src/sync/state.ts.

Advisory (Q2). The 409 step-down in `pushUnderContract` mirrors the inline step-down in inbound.ts `fetchPage`. Both already share `acceptableContract`. What remains is the surrounding steps, written twice. Kept as advisory, as the reviewer filed it.
Advisory (Q2, boilerplate). The bare-404 branch (`setContract(…, 1)` then `contractRefusal()`) is written three times.
Advisory (Q10). The comment says a row with no id adopts the server's id silently, but no code writes that id.
Advisory (Q5). No code in src/ reads `ALIAS_KINDS`, so the claim that a new kind is one entry does not hold. AC-38 requires the export itself.
Advisory (Q8, unused export). The re-export of `NAME_STATES` and `nameFlagKey` is unused outside a test.
Advisory (Q9). The guard can never be reached because of the types, but it throws loudly, so it hides nothing.
Advisory (Q5). `as !== null` is tested again although `naming` already contains it.
Advisory (Q5). `prefixLength` rebuilds a key only to read its length.
Advisory (Q5). `currentItemsUnder` only forwards to `nameCountsOf`.
Advisory (Q3/Q6). The contract that brought shared names is a bare `2` in several files, with no named constant.
Advisory (Q6). The imported count prints twice and without `plural()`, so one memory reads '1 imported memories'.
Advisory (Q2). `levelPhrase` and the join question copy the CLI's text. `hasField` is repeated inline in the template.
Advisory (Q9). When the given id is already in use, the route quietly makes a new id. No criterion covers this case. Kept as advisory, as filed.

Advisory (Q11). The rewritten Known-limits paragraph still promises that the next bump pins the refusal shape, and this change is that bump. It is the same matter that architecture F-1 upholds as a defect.
Advisory (Q11). The new withdrawal sentence leaves out the held-withdrawal case. It agrees with ADR 0027.
Advisory, debt. The diff did not write this line ('a 409 on the contract stops it'), so it is outside the change.

Upheld (Q1). AC-44 promises the CLI prints the imported count when it is above 0 (src/cli/commands/share.ts:289, :308). I checked: 'imported' does not appear in share-names-cli.test.ts or sharing-cli.test.ts, so removing both lines passes every test.

Upheld (Q1). AC-41 promises that a full sweep reads `/v1/me` again for a row below CONTRACT. The tests call `refreshContracts(ctx, { onlyBelow: true })` directly. No test drives the tick's full-sweep branch at src/sync/run.ts:347; the `sync --once` test passes through `startSteps`. Removing that line passes every test.

Upheld (Q1). AC-41 says 'the lower of CONTRACT and' the server's answer. Every test server answers 1 or 2, never above CONTRACT, so storing the server's value as-is (join.ts:164, run.ts:103, binding.ts:207) would pass. A server at `{ current: 3 }` would catch it.

Upheld (Q1). AC-28 requires `REASON_TEXT['unbound-alias']` (src/sharing/types.ts:125-126) to say 'git remote or shared name'. I checked: tests pin the policy's sentence (sharing-policy.test.ts:238) but not this one, so putting back the old sentence passes.

Upheld (Q1). AC-42 promises that a snapshot without a teammate's memory under the name forgets it. The only snapshot case (line 313) is the re-created one, which asserts rows are kept. Widening the filter at src/sync/inbound.ts:789-790 to skip every name alias would still pass.
Upheld (Q1). AC-39 promises `limit` clamped to 1..200. With 60 names seeded, `?limit=500` returning 60 proves no upper clamp; a maximum of 60 or more, or none at all, passes.

Upheld (Q3). An existing assertion for remote-bound projects was inverted: naming another remote alias used to rebind, and now the bound alias is kept until Nothing. The change follows spec D-1 ('the bound alias wins'). But AC-3 states the no-rebind rule only for a shared name, and AC-47 names only this file's `no-remote` cases as changed. So the preserve criterion's list does not cover this case, and no behavior criterion proves the new rule for remotes. Name it in AC-47 and state it in a behavior criterion.
Advisory (Q1, partial). The no-request check counts only one URL, so a `/v1/me` read or a POST would go unseen.
Advisory. The test does not tell parallel reads from sequential ones, and the unstopped filter is not exercised.
Advisory (Q2). 'A remote is never listed' holds by construction of the fixture.
Advisory. The no-SQL check searches the source for two call shapes only. The order 'after `purged`' is not tested.
Advisory (Q2). The test asserts the text of another test file; the boundary test itself is the proof.
Advisory (Q5). The test asserts `statusReport`, not the CLI's `--json` output.
Advisory. AC-43 names `GET /api/projects`, but the route is `/api/overview`. The test follows the code; the criterion's text is wrong.
Advisory. Edge cases the plan lists were not written: the 101st name, no D-10 hold on a `name` refusal, and `one-server` at the CLI.
Advisory. Several edited assertions are not named in AC-47, but each follows a change a criterion states.
Dropped, recorded as advisory. The finding names criterion AC-46, not a line of the diff. The reviewer itself found that the 'documents' reason mostly holds.
Advisory, debt. The old reason-text test checks only that each sentence ends with a full stop.
Advisory, debt. The old substring assertion 'no git remote' does not pin the new `no-name` advice.
Advisory. Any member can re-create a lost name with a known id. As the reviewer states, this is no widening of what members could already do.
Advisory. A purged name keeps its creator and alias in `team.db`. ADR 0028 states the limit, and only the operator can see it.
Advisory. The server's contract is stored without an integer check. A bad value fails closed (`contract` stop).
Advisory, debt. Any member may pull any alias (ADR 0026 D-11). This is unchanged by the diff.

Upheld (Q2, undeclared reachable branch), on the diff-line branch: review/ui-evidence.json is absent, so the manifest cannot stand as the evidence. The diff adds dock branches a person can reach that are not among the 14 declared states. A capture cannot show a state nobody declared, so only the diff shows them. I checked each in the code: the `refused` sentence (line 203), the purged-at-confirm sentence (line 344, starting lowercase), the created-name sentence after a refusal, 'The list shows the first 1,000 names.' (line 542), and the 'Not changed' toasts (lines 298, 357). The gap is in the spec's state list.

Upheld (Q2, undeclared reachable branch), on the diff-line branch. `nameStateLabel` (line 67) adds '· missing on the server', '· re-created by <member>' and '· removed by the operator' to each name line. The page declares only `names` and `held`, and every captured name line is in the ok state, so no capture can show these suffixes.
Advisory (Q5). Raw Markdown backticks show in the dock's sentences, while the bound sentences render the same slug as code (projects-taken@1280-dark.png).
Advisory (Q5). The named-nothing sentence tells the person they would join a name their own member created, with no 'you'.
Advisory. In the dark scheme, the disabled field in the held state looks the same as the enabled one.
Advisory. The spec says the bound field stays read-only; the build removes it. The result reads clearly.
Advisory (Q7, crowding that holds). The name line wraps badly at 360px but stays readable.
Advisory, debt. At 768px the list column collapses with the dock open. This is list code the diff did not touch.
Advisory, debt. The server pill stays a green 'Ok' while names are held. The diff did not touch the pill.
Advisory. A missing name is re-sent on every sweep with no backoff. The only signal is the `missing` flag.
Advisory. `serve purge name` has no dry run and no undo, so a mistyped alias retires a live name.
Advisory. The runbook's Rollback section does not say that names created since are lost. ADR 0026 and ADR 0028 do state the rollback.
Advisory. After a restore older than a name, a Receive-only teammate's copies are dropped with nothing on their side to explain it.
Advisory, as filed. The client rollback is stated in the spec and in ADR 0028, so no rollback is missing. What is left is that the release notes owe a sentence, and that falls to the release item.
Advisory, debt. A stale `serve.lease` makes the new image restart repeatedly until the lease expires.
Advisory, debt. An older binary refuses the version 8 store and its hooks fail open. Every store bump has carried this risk.

Upheld (Q3, a contract changed without its file). `POST /v1/names` answers 409 `{ error: 'exists', name: <NameItemShape> }`. The client relies on `name`: src/sync/binding.ts:379 reads `made.body.name`. The base says `CONTRACT_FINGERPRINT` pins the key lists and result shapes, yet `RESULT_SHAPES.refusal` (src/team/contract.ts:107) stays `['error','instance','serverId']`. ADR 0027:102 also promised that this bump would pin `accepted`. Pin the 409 bodies the client reads and repin the fingerprint, or record in ADR 0028 why the debt carries forward.
Advisory. Nothing reads `ALIAS_KINDS`, so the 'one entry' claim does not hold. The same point appears in code-quality F-6.
Advisory. The names-held rule is recomputed with a literal 2 instead of reading `heldByContract` or `namesHeld`.
Advisory. The literal `/^name:/` prefix sits outside the identity leaf.
Advisory. `nameId` is typed as required, but a contract-1 server never sends it.
Advisory. The build reads the Design differently: the items are assembled in routes.ts, per row. No boundary is crossed, because the SQL stays in store.ts.
Advisory. The new `slugCore` export is not recorded in ADR 0028, and names.ts is called a leaf although it imports entry.ts.
Advisory. The sharing store now writes `project_aliases`. The Design asks for this, but ADR 0028 does not say it.
Advisory, debt. The `accepted` and `retryAfterSec` gap dates from contract 1. The new part is upheld above.
Advisory, debt. Inline project-name lookups have no shared helper, and the new `share status` copies the pattern.
Advisory (Q1/Q6). `clearServerLedger` leaves the `names.<state>` meta flags behind, and they come back if the same server id is added again.
Advisory (Q2). `importedStayCounts` filters on `origin` with no index, a full pass on each preview. The result is correct.
Advisory (Q2). Each listed name costs up to three indexed queries.
Advisory (Q2). `receivedNameCounts` filters on `remote_alias` with no index and reads the same rows twice.
Advisory (Q5). The creator columns are kept forever after a purge, and ADR 0028 does not name them.
Advisory, debt. A restore does not clear the `names.%` flags. The same point as F-1.
